questions.stem: Which set matches all four direct connections in the five-node drawing?
assumptions: Read connectivity only; the figure gives no publication direction, topic name or message type.

citations.locator: Lecture 5, physical PDF page 183, printed slide 13: relevant text, equations and associated figures
citations.evidenceText:
ROS Node: The Atomic Unit of Computation

•  A Node is a single-purpose programming module or a
   process that performs computation.                       Came
                                                                                                                            Lidar             Control
                                                                                                     ra•   In a ROS-based robot, you do not write one massive                   Node           Node                                                                            Node
   program; instead, you write many small programs
   (python scripts) called nodes.
                                                                              SLAM            Nav•  These Multiple small programs (nodes) work together
                                                                                   Node            Node
   using ROS functionalities.
•  The core idea behind nodes is “divide and simplify”.
•  Features of Node:
    –  Single Responsibility: Each node should do one thing well.
       For example, one node might read images from a camera,
       while another node performs AI object detection, and a
        third node sends commands to the motor controller.


                                                                                                          13

solution.justification: The visible lines connect Camera to Lidar and SLAM, and Lidar to Control and Nav; there are no arrowheads or topic labels.

optionExplanations.o1: This matches the four visible line segments.
optionExplanations.o2: This swaps the lower branches: Camera connects to SLAM, and Lidar connects to Nav.
optionExplanations.o3: The upper-left segment joins Camera to Lidar, not directly to Control.
optionExplanations.o4: Neither SLAM–Nav nor Camera–Control is drawn as a direct connection.

solution.simpleExplanation: The visible lines connect Camera to Lidar and SLAM, and Lidar to Control and Nav; there are no arrowheads or topic labels.
misconceptions: This swaps the lower branches: Camera connects to SLAM, and Lidar connects to Nav.
The upper-left segment joins Camera to Lidar, not directly to Control.
Neither SLAM–Nav nor Camera–Control is drawn as a direct connection.

questions.stem: Large video frames are moving from a hardware driver to an AI node. Which measurement most directly assesses the slide’s aim of reducing the cost of that data movement?
assumptions: Assess the source’s motivation, not an exact bandwidth measurement or a guarantee that every deployment uses zero-copy transfer.

options.text: Time spent on CNN inference after the frame is already available to the AI node
Time spent on camera exposure before the frame data is available to the driver
Time spent applying a motor command after navigation has selected it
Time and processing overhead for transferring each frame between those components

citations.locator: Lecture 5, physical PDF page 190, printed slide 20: relevant text, equations and associated figures
citations.evidenceText:
ROS Messages: Standardizing the Language

• Nodes must speak the same language to communicate. In ROS,
   this "language" is the Message.
   – Message Types (Interfaces): A message is a strictly defined data structure
         (e.g., an integer, a string, or a complex array of pixels).
   – Common AI Messages:
             • sensor_msgs/Image: Used for raw camera data.
             • geometry_msgs/Twist: Used for movement commands (Linear and Angular velocity).
   – Jetson handles high-bandwidth messages, like 4K
       video streams, using optimized ROS message
       structures that minimize the "cost" of moving data
      between AI nodes and hardware drivers.



                                                                                                          20

solution.justification: The stated optimization targets the overhead of moving high-bandwidth data between components, so measure that transfer rather than a different stage.

optionExplanations.o1: This directly measures the data-transfer stage named by the source.
optionExplanations.o2: Inference is a different computation after the transfer has supplied the frame.
optionExplanations.o3: Exposure occurs before the data-transfer stage being assessed.
optionExplanations.o4: Motor actuation occurs in a different downstream stage.

solution.simpleExplanation: Measure the transfer stage itself, not acquisition, inference or actuation.
misconceptions: Inference is a different computation after the transfer has supplied the frame.
Exposure occurs before the data-transfer stage being assessed.
Motor actuation occurs in a different downstream stage.

                                               –  Request–Response → call_async(req)
